Nearly 90% of the world’s population was eliminated, driving the survivors to band together into loose communities and tribes. In Arctic Scavengers, you are the leader of a small tribe of survivors. Resources, tools, medicine, and mercenaries are all in scarce supply. You and your tribe are pitted against up to four other tribes in a fight for survival. Build up your tribe, skirmish against other players head-to-head, or even bluff your way to victory. The player with the largest tribe at the end of the game is declared the winner! Setup Each player starts with: 4 refugee cards 3 scavenger cards 1 brawler card 1 spear card 1 shovel card Playing the Game Each round of Arctic Scavengers has three phases, played in the order shown below: Drawing Phase 1) Discard all cards from the previous round. 2) Each player draws 5 cards from the top of their deck, shuffling the discard pile and adding it to the deck when their deck becomes exhausted. 3) Beginning with the third round, and continuing for the remainder of the game, the initiator peeks at the top card on the contested resources pile and then returns it to the pile. Resource Gathering Phase 4) The initiator takes the first action and uses any number of cards to gather resources. 5) The initiator announces how many of their cards will remain for the skirmish. 6) Play continues with the other players, in clockwise order, and they execute steps 4 and 5. Skirmish Phase (Round 3 and following) 7) Once all players have taken their resource gathering actions, players reveal their remaining cards for the skirmish and a winner is determined. 8) The winner of the skirmish takes the top card from the contested resources pile and adds it to their discard pile. 9) The initiator passes the initiator card to their left-hand opponent, starting a new round. The game continues like this until the contested resource pile is depleted. Resource Gathering During this phase, each player plays any number of cards from their hand in order to add more resources (cards) to their deck. Gathering starts with the player that has the initiator card (lying in their play area) and play continues in clockwise order. There is no limit to the number of actions that a player can take during the resource gathering phase, although no action may be taken more than once. Dig The player draws one or more cards from the top of the junkyard pile. The player may choose one to place in their discard pile and returns any other cards to the bottom of the junkyard pile. The number of cards is determined by the sum of all the dig numbers displayed on the card(s) played from the player’s hand. As with other actions, dig may only be used once per round. Draw The player draws one or more cards from their deck, adding them to their hand. Multiple cards may be combined to draw several cards. As with other actions, draw may only be used once per round. Hire The hire ability is a free action (no card is needed to grant this action) in which a player takes a mercenary card from the face-up piles of cards. [Rating: 2/10] To be honest.. The game play was just boring and dull even along with the skirmishes.. so much many better deck building games other than this..

[Rating: 2/10] I appreciate that Scavengers tries to be a deckbuilder in moderation, as opposed to something outlandish and broken, but the game is just dull, really. There's not much going on - not many different cards to draft and not much to do with what you've drafted. Some of the mechanics work; for example, only being able to do one draw action per turn, so that card-draw isn't just free deck slots. Or trashing cards whenever you feel like it, instead of using them. But the other actions are pretty janky, it's just buy stuff if you can or save up and pray for the skirmish. [Rating: 2/10] yet another deck builder trying to do far too much at the once. there are too many different types of action and the actions are limited to once a turn, making drawing a 'good hand' objectively impossible. Limiting to only one buy each turn is pretty ridiculous as if you manage to eventually draw a hand with a strong buy power, you can only get one of those things. When I play a deck builder, my aim is to make a consistent deck, so I can have fun playing cards. This game is designed to make consistency impossible and has more 'feel bad' turns than any other deckbuilder i've player.

[Rating: 2/10] Solo play.   Written review: http://www.beyondsolitaire.net/blog/solo-review-arctic-scavengers-base-game-hq-recon

[Rating: 2/10] Very bad sensation on this game. Many better deck building games. Need luck otherwise the game is really boring.

[Rating: 2.5/10] Clone of Dominion with a twist meant to increase player interaction at the expense of adding a significant amount of luck (blind bidding for an unknown card). I would always choose to play Dominion over this game.

[Rating: 3/10] A sad little Dominion knock-off that is far too random to be any fun. Probably should have been play-tested more to balance out the inevitable inequity between players.

[Rating: 3/10] Played one full game, and one abandoned game after getting the rules wrong. The rule book is garbage and you will definitely need the FAQ to meaningfully play this game. This game just feels supper fiddly with lots of eminently forgettable rules. There are also some mechanics that don't seem 100% logical - I'm still not totally sure how snipers and saboteurs work even after reading the FAQ. There are plenty of more tightly designed deck builders like Dominion, Trains and Ascension that I would rather play. [Rating: 3/10] It's just a clunkier, slower, more luck based, less balanced Dominion. Pointless.

[Rating: 3/10] The rules were clunky for a game that is light on choices.  Too many mechanics have a high luck factor.  Several cards are directed spite, which I find unsavory in a multi-player game.  Given that it was an early deck builder, these errors are understandable but still stopped me from enjoying it.

[Rating: 3/10] Solid but slightly vanilla feeling deckbuilder. the skirmish isn't as tense as I expected, since there is little reason not to "bluff", and no cost for not succeeding. Enjoyed, will play again, but not a world-shaker.  Update: not sure I have the patience for deckbuilders. This one drags and the much lauded "interaction" is dull and pointless. Dropping my rating.
